To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thickness of the protective coating on the reinforcement of a reinforced concrete structure is an important factor that influences the corrosion process of the steel, and that the external manifestation of this corrosion process (cracking of coating) depends on the thickness of the protection and on the mechanical requests to which the structure is subjected.
the thickness of the concrete coating of the reinforcing steel is a key factor in the resistance to corrosion of reinforced concrete structures.
the thickness of the concrete cover has a great influence on the corrosion process in the reinforced concrete beams subjected to flexion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of external loads on the corrosion process of reinforced concrete beams with different coating thickness of the steel bars.
the influence of the thickness of coating of the reinforcement of reinforced concrete beams subjected to an accelerated corrosion and to external flexural effects.

the influence of coating thicknesses of the reinforcement of 0, 0.15, and 0.30 mm, on the corrosion process of a reinforced concrete beam, subjected to flexural effects and with a concrete strength of 25 MP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thickness of the concrete coating of the reinforcement is a key factor in the corrosion of reinforced concrete.
, in general, the thicker the coating thickness, the more resistant to corrosion the reinforced concrete element.
the coating of the reinforcement has a positive influence on the resistance of the structure to cracking, and that the thicker the coating is, the greater the resistance is.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the thickness of the concrete covering the reinforcement is not only an important parameter for the service life of reinforced concrete elements, but it is also a parameter that influences the corrosion process and the external manifestations of the corrosion.

the thicker coating of the reinforcement is, the more resistant it is against the corrosion process, which translates to a greater resistance of the structure against the external loads and a lower manifestation of the corrosion process on the external coating.

a greater coating thickness of the elements of the reinforcement of the concrete, in addition to the protection against corrosion of the steel, allows to delay the cracking of the concrete due to the action of the external loads, which can be translated into a greater service life of the structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coating thickness of reinforcement is an essential parameter to consider when studying corrosion in reinforced concrete structures.

, for the same mechanical request and the same concrete resistance, an increase in the thickness of the reinforcement coating will delay the appearance of the first cracks and the subsequent corrosion process.
the coating thickness of reinforced concrete has a significant influence on the corrosion process of the reinforcement and its external manifestation.
